_readme: Copy to a file outside the repo and point config.ini's accounts_file at it.
Order matters: the first account is the primary. It is the only one that
authenticates to the TeleDrive backend (the bot challenge proves the drive
owner's identity), and it is the account a row with telegram_user_id 0 --
everything registered before multi-account support -- is read back from.
Every other account must already be linked to the same drive on the web
client, or it is read-only here: the pool will serve its existing files but
will not route new uploads to it.
telegram_user_id must match the account the session actually belongs to;
a mismatch disables that one account and says so, and leaves the rest up.
session takes a Telethon StringSession (TeleDrive's generate_session.py).
It stays on this machine: only MTProto ever sees it, never the backend.
Keep the real file out of version control and off pastebins -- a session
string is the whole Telegram account, not a password that can be rotated.
